Research developing autocomplete capabilities for for ddflow cli commands and ID and options and create phase and tasks to impenet this

data.claim: A stdlib-only, generated completion works: (1) static command/option tree is exported from build_parser() into per-shell scripts (bash, zsh, fish) at install/upgrade time; (2) IDs come from a read-only sqlite3 query of .ddflow/index.db-* items table, not from running ddflow; (3) argcomplete is not adopted as a runtime dependency. A per-TAB 'ddflow' subprocess is not viable.
data.falsifier: If a bash/zsh completion that shells out to python -c 'import sqlite3' still exceeds ~100 ms per TAB, or if the newest-index heuristic offers stale ids in a repo with several index files, the sqlite approach fails and a pre-generated ids cache file refreshed by the post-merge hook is needed.
data.mechanism: ddflow is pure argparse (SuggestingParser, build_parser() in surfaces/cli.py, subcommands registered from surfaces/parsers/*, compat aliases via _WordsRecorder/_hide_from_abbreviation). pyproject declares exactly two runtime deps (jinja2, tomlkit) by policy; argcomplete and shtab are not installed. 'ddflow --version' takes ~1.0 s and importing ddflow.surfaces.cli ~0.83 s (ddflow.api imports dominate), 'ddflow list/show' ~4.7 s on this loaded machine, so argcomplete-style per-TAB invocation would add 1-5 s per keypress. The derived index .ddflow/index.db-<code fingerprint> is plain sqlite: items(id,kind,title,state,needs,tags,...) 3488 rows, count query 0.0 s, openable read-only with stdlib sqlite3. Index name embeds code_fingerprint(), so a stale file can exist; the completer must pick the newest by mtime or fall back to nothing.

data.question: How should ddflow offer shell completion (commands, options, IDs) given its argparse CLI, two-runtime-dependency policy and slow startup?
sources: ddflow/surfaces/cli.py build_parser; ddflow/surfaces/registry.py; pyproject.toml dependencies; ddflow/infra/store.py index.db naming

data.body: Research R-shell-completion-design. Stdlib only (two-runtime-dependency policy): a command tree exported from build_parser(), generated scripts per shell, IDs read from the derived sqlite index without importing ddflow.api (startup is ~1 s), install only with the operator's consent. Every new CLI verb touches golden snapshots, README tables and pins: run 'pytest tests/test_scenarios.py -m slow' and 'ddflow pins regenerate --check' before merge.
data.title: Shell completion: commands, options, values and IDs for bash, zsh and fish

data.body: Ask the operator, with defaults: (1) shells: bash+zsh+fish (default) or bash only first; (2) install: explicit 'ddflow completion install' plus a doctor note, never automatic (default); (3) stdlib-only generated scripts (default, per R-shell-completion-design) vs argcomplete as an optional extra; (4) ID source: read-only sqlite of .ddflow/index.db-* (default) vs a cache file refreshed by the post-merge hook; (5) which values complete: ids of every record kind, enums, gate names, phases, agents. Record each answer as D-completion-*.
data.title: DECIDE: shell completion scope, install policy and ID source (operator questions with defaults)

data.body: Pure function parser -> JSON-able tree: subcommand words (incl. compat aliases but not hidden old flags per _hide_from_abbreviation), options with arity and choices, and a value kind per argument (id:task|bug|phase|..., enum, path, free). Walks argparse internals once; no side effects; no import of ddflow.api beyond parser building. Tests: every option of every real subcommand appears; hidden/compat flags are not offered; stable ordering.
data.title: Export the CLI command tree from build_parser(): commands, options, choices, aliases, value kinds

data.body: New verb 'ddflow completion SHELL' prints a script to stdout (managed templates under ddflow/templates/completion, one per shell, each under 20 KB). Commands and options complete from the embedded tree with no ddflow subprocess; value kinds call the fast ID helper. Tests run bash and zsh -c with a faked COMP_WORDS where those shells exist, otherwise record unavailable. Regenerate golden snapshots, README command table and pins.
data.title: ddflow completion <bash|zsh|fish>: generate the completion script from the tree

data.body: Stdlib-only module opened read-only (sqlite3 file:...?mode=ro) on the newest .ddflow/index.db-* by mtime (the name embeds code_fingerprint(), so several can exist); items.id by kind/state, bugs, research, decisions, lessons; finds the primary checkout from a worktree. Returns nothing (never an error) when no index exists. Budget test: cold python start plus query under 100 ms on this repo's 3.5k items, via python -S -c. Falsifier from R-shell-completion-design: if it exceeds the budget, fall back to a cache file refreshed by the post-merge hook.
data.title: Fast value helper: ids, states, phases, gates from the sqlite index in under 100 ms without importing ddflow.api

data.body: Map each option and positional to a value kind in the tree and complete it: record ids by kind (task show/claim/complete/gate ..., bug show/fixed, phase), enum choices from argparse, gate names from the configured pipeline, phases and tags, files and directories for path options. Positional id completion must respect the verb (claim offers open items; bug fixed offers open bugs).

data.text: Research the ability to add security gate to the default phase gates to research for security bugs and issues, dependency upgrades and checks, compliance to security policies and corporate security policies and add this as phase and tasks to work on

data.claim: Yes. ddflow has NO security gate today (ddflow gate list: research rules implement rubber_duck critic verify standards ci unit_tests bug_hunt dedupe live_test docs corrections tasks merge). The machinery needed already exists: GateDef (applies_to task|phase|both, applies_when path globs, requires_evidence, mutations, reviewer family), custom gates in .ddflow/gates.toml, a [gates] task_pipeline list, companions, layered config with company-enforced floors (D-config-layer-order), graded policies (P-graded-policies) and waivers (D-DEP-Q8). The work is a new GateDef plus one shared scanner runner, finding-to-bug filing and a policy checklist, not a new engine. It must reuse the scanners the ci gate already runs instead of adding a second copy.
data.falsifier: If B-security-pass already specifies and is about to ship the same gate (its blockers P-unify, SC-catalogue close soon), a new phase duplicates it and the right move is to extend that item; if a new 'security' gate in the default task_pipeline makes every unit-test-only change wait on scanners that are unavailable on most machines, applies_when scoping and the unavailable-not-passed rule must keep it from stalling the queue.
data.mechanism: Security checks exist but outside ddflow's gates: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs gitleaks 8.30.1 (full history), bandit -r ddflow/ -ll (package only), pip-audit --strict whose failure is only a warning (|| echo ::warning), and CodeQL security-and-quality; the ci gate runs the pre-commit stages (D-ci-parity-r2) so bandit and gitleaks happen there but a result is just pass/fail with no severity, no finding record and no policy or dependency-upgrade view. Prior queue items overlap strongly and must not be duplicated: B-security-pass (operator 2026-09-28: phase-level security gate, cadence, SAST/secret/CVE/image scanners as companions; blocked on P-unify, SC-catalogue), B-dependency-upgrades, B-security-pass-sync, B-export-security-md (SECURITY.md), B-pi-review-lens (security review lens as data), B-par-phase-barrier, IA-supply-chain, IA-compliance, GV-guardrails, GP-org and CM-packs (company policy packs pinned by digest), P-deprecation (security exceptions need severity=security and a lesson). Note .ddflow/config.toml pins task_pipeline literally, so a packaged-default gate does not reach this project until that list is amended.

data.question: Can ddflow add a default 'security' gate covering security bugs and issues, dependency checks and upgrades, and compliance with security policies including corporate ones, and what already exists to build on?

data.body: Research R-security-gate-design. Adds a default 'security' gate to the task and phase pipelines. Reuse, do not duplicate: the scanners ci already runs (bandit, gitleaks, pip-audit) move behind ONE shared runner that both the gate and ci call; SECURITY-related queue items B-security-pass (phase-level gate, cadence, companions), B-dependency-upgrades, B-security-pass-sync, B-export-security-md, B-pi-review-lens (security lens) and IA-supply-chain overlap this phase: SEC-decide asks the operator whether this phase supersedes or absorbs them, and nothing here edits those items. A scanner that cannot run is recorded unavailable, never passed. Corporate policy rides the company layer (D-config-layer-order): tighten-only floors, expiring waivers (D-DEP-Q8). This project pins [gates].task_pipeline literally in .ddflow/config.toml, so the gate must also be added there.
data.title: Security gate: scan for security issues, check and upgrade dependencies, enforce security and corporate policy

data.body: Ask the operator, with defaults: (1) pipeline: security gate in BOTH task and phase pipelines, scoped by applies_when to code, dependency manifests and CI/workflow files (default); (2) position: after standards, before ci (default); (3) blocking: high and critical findings block, medium and low are recorded as bugs (default), pip-audit findings block instead of warn-only; (4) scanners as companions with consent: bandit or semgrep (SAST), gitleaks (secrets), pip-audit or osv-scanner (CVE) (default); (5) dependency upgrades: propose as tasks, never auto-apply (default); (6) corporate policy comes from the company layer/pack, tighten-only; (7) B-security-pass, B-dependency-upgrades, B-security-pass-sync: absorb into this phase and close them as superseded (default) or keep and make this phase depend on them. Record each answer as D-security-*.
data.title: DECIDE: security gate scope, blocking thresholds, scanner set, corporate policy source and fate of B-security-pass (operator questions with defaults)

data.body: GateDef security: applies_to both, applies_when scoped globs (**/*.py, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, requirements*, package*.json, Dockerfile*, .github/**), needs_branch, requires_evidence report+fields (scanners_run, findings_by_severity, policy_checked). Added to the packaged task_pipeline and phase_pipeline; this project's literal [gates].task_pipeline in .ddflow/config.toml updated too. All thresholds are knobs ([security].block_severity etc., settable four ways, logged). Register a mutation so 'ddflow gate verify <item> security' proves it can go red. Update golden snapshots, README tables, pins.
data.title: Add the 'security' GateDef to the default task and phase pipelines, with [security] knobs and gate verify mutation

data.body: Single implementation (reuse-core rule): bandit/semgrep, gitleaks, pip-audit/osv-scanner run through cmdrunner, output normalized to {tool, rule, severity, file, line, advisory id}. The ci gate and the security gate call it; CI workflow and pre-commit stay equal to it (tests like tests/test_gitleaks_config.py). Companion entries with consent-gated install hints; a missing tool is recorded unavailable, never passed. pip-audit blocks per [security] knob instead of '|| echo ::warning'.
data.title: One shared scanner runner and companions: SAST, secrets and dependency CVEs, normalized to findings; ci calls the same runner

data.body: Report known advisories (CVE/GHSA with affected and fixed-in versions), outdated direct dependencies, unpinned or unhashed requirements, and missing lockfile; propose each upgrade as a task or bug tagged security/dependency with the risk (major bump, transitive), never auto-applied. Feeds B-dependency-upgrades if it survives SEC-decide. The dependency allowlist hook already in pre-commit is consulted, not duplicated.
data.title: Dependency checks and upgrade proposals: advisories, outdated pins, lockfile and license hygiene, proposed as tasks

data.body: Security policies are managed rules with a strength (recommended, required, forbidden per P-graded-policies) from project and company layers; the gate renders a checklist (secrets handling, input validation, authn/authz, logging of sensitive data, supply chain) the agent must answer with evidence and a cross-family reviewer checks via the security lens (B-pi-review-lens). A project cannot weaken a company floor (D-config-layer-order); an exception is an expiring recorded waiver with a reason (D-DEP-Q8).
data.title: Security and corporate policy compliance: policy records, checklist with evidence, company floors and expiring waivers

data.body: Each unwaived finding at or above the knob severity is recorded as a bug tagged security with scanner evidence (deduped by fingerprint, not by line), gets a fix task, and cannot close without a regression test that fails on the unfixed code. Accepted risk = waiver record with owner, reason and expiry; an expired waiver reopens the finding. Optional hook toward B-security-pass-sync (SECURITY.md).
data.title: Findings become bugs: severity, dedupe, regression test, accepted-risk waivers with expiry

data.body: Run the gate at phase completion and on a cadence (knob: every N phases or days) through the existing cadence mechanism; doctor reports the last security run and unavailable scanners; operator digest lists open security bugs and expiring waivers. Coordinates with B-par-phase-barrier and B-security-pass per SEC-decide.
data.title: Phase-level and periodic security runs, doctor lines and digest entries

data.body: Scenarios: seeded hardcoded secret, seeded vulnerable pinned dependency and seeded policy violation each block the gate and file a bug; a missing scanner records unavailable; a project layer cannot lower a company floor; a waiver expires and reopens; gate verify security goes red on the registered mutation. Run 'pytest tests/test_scenarios.py -m slow' (a default-pipeline change) and 'ddflow pins regenerate --check'.
data.title: End to end: a seeded vulnerability is caught, an unavailable scanner is not a pass, a company floor holds

data.body: Document the gate, scanners and their consent-gated install, knobs and thresholds, corporate policy layering, waivers, how it relates to ci and to SECURITY.md. README is ddflow-managed: follow its generated-table rules.
data.title: Docs: README row, 'ddflow help security' topic and security gate guide
